backend: offline committed resources only; no network, no GPU
gap_before_this_change: ExperimentCampaignV1.locked_eval_manifest_sha256 and CampaignResultV1.locked_eval_manifest_sha256 are free-form 64-hex-char strings validated only for pattern shape and self-consistency (manifest.locked_eval_manifest_sha256 == result.locked_eval_manifest_sha256). Neither was ever checked against real bytes of the committed manifest file. tests/test_autoresearch/test_experiment_campaign.py's own fixture used the literal digest "e"*64, which does not correspond to any manifest -- and validate_result_claim already returned () (no failures) for it.

recompute_declared_digest.method: load_locked_manifest_payload(canonical_manifest_path()) recomputes sha256({schema, rows, metadata}) with the same canonical json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) encoding LockedManifest.sha256 uses, and fails closed if it does not equal the file's own manifest_sha256 field
recompute_declared_digest.result: recomputed digest equals declared digest: true

honesty.scope: governance/gate wiring audit only -- no model quality, promotion, or training result is claimed here
honesty.backward_compatibility: locked_manifest_path defaults to None everywhere it was threaded (validate_result_claim, CampaignStore.validate_campaign_result, evaluate_promotion, register_promoted_checkpoint, load_campaign_governance); every existing caller and test that never passed it keeps its prior (self-consistency-only) behavior unchanged. No canonical default path is wired in yet -- callers that want the stronger check must opt in with locked_eval_manifest.canonical_manifest_path().
